chunks: And from him, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
"The Muhrim (person in Ihram) should not dip his whole body in the water." As for covering the head, it indicates that what he narrated is permissible:

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The pilgrim in the state of Ihram
key_terms.يَرْتَمِسُ: To fully submerge or dip the whole body in water

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on bathing for a pilgrim in the state of Ihram?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the specific prohibition of *irtimas* (full submersion) for the Muhrim, distinguishing it from general washing. Shaykh al-Tusi includes this in the chapter on prohibitions to resolve juristic debates regarding whether the restriction applies to the entire body or specifically to the head and feet, ultimately indicating that full immersion is discouraged or prohibited while partial washing is permitted.
